newsitem.title: USA: Rising water shifts focus downriver on Mississippi.
newsitem.headline: Rising water shifts focus downriver on Mississippi.

text.p: River officials have shifted their attention to rising water levels on a section of the Mississippi River from Dubuque, Iowa south to Chester, Ill. as water on upper reaches of the Mississippi slowly falls.
"From Dubuque, Iowa to Chester Illinois, there is the highest water levels area now," said Bob Hildebrand, chief warrant officer, Coast Guard Marine Safety Office at St Louis.
He confirmed water on the upper Mississippi River was starting to fall from LaCrosse, Wis. northward.
Water levels also were easing near Minneapolis and St Paul, Minn, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The Mississippi River at Minneapolis has dropped two feet to 14.4 feet, below the 16 foot flood stage and was slowly falling. At St Paul, the water was still at 21.5 feet, above the 14-foot flood stage but it was also slowly receding and flowing down the river, Hildebrand said.
Downriver at Davenport, Iowa, water levels Wednesday stood at 18 feet, three feet above the 15-foot flood stage and was seen cresting by Friday if no weather changes occur, he said.
Also, the Mississippi River at St Louis was at 29.6 feet, just below the 30-foot flood stage and was expected to crest there by Friday at 32 to 33 feet, he added.
